chunks: As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Abi Usamah or someone else, who said:
One time I climbed Mount Abi Qubays while the people were performing salat al-Maghrib, and I saw that the sun had not set; rather, it had only become hidden behind the mountain from the people.
Then I met Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام while he was praying, and I informed him of that. So he said to me: Why did you do that? What you did was evil.
We only perform it when we no longer see it above the mountain—when it has disappeared or gone down—so long as clouds have not covered it or a darkness has not obscured it.
Rather, your responsibility is only your own east and your own west, and the people are not required to investigate.

key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: salat al-Maghrib, the sunset prayer under discussion here
key_terms.تَوَارَتْ: became hidden from sight, without necessarily indicating absolute astronomical disappearance
key_terms.سَحَابٌ: cloud cover that may obstruct direct observation of the sun
key_terms.غَابَتْ: set or disappeared from visible sight
key_terms.مَشْرِقُكَ: your eastern horizon or orientational point of sunrise in your locality
key_terms.مَغْرِبُكَ: your western horizon or orientational point of sunset in your locality
key_terms.يَبْحَثُوا: to investigate or probe beyond ordinary obligation

ai.seo_question: When does the time of salat al-Maghrib begin according to this hadith from al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns the time of salat al-Maghrib and teaches that the practical criterion is the disappearance of the sun from the observer's visible horizon, not investigation beyond ordinary sight. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام reproves excessive scrutiny and indicates that people are to act according to what is normally observable in their own locality unless clouds or darkness interfere.
